requests.title: 悬在头顶的海 · 世界意象
requests.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset for the independent cosmic-horror extraction game "After That Day". Create an original environment concept; no text, labels, HUD, watermark, frame, panel collage or logo. Quiet existential dread after a completed reality-overwriting catastrophe, a vulnerable ordinary human carrying a small warm shoulder lamp and a crowbar. The alien world's native processes are still running, distorted by an incompatible physical law. No combat hero pose. No human buildings, industrial props, occult symbols, tentacle decoration, eyes everywhere, neon emissive outlines, shiny sci-fi platforms. Strong material specificity, carefully designed silhouettes, believable weight and atmospheric scale. Landscape 3:2.
Wide atmospheric establishing image from near a tiny human on a dry abyssal seabed. Above them, an ENTIRE dark deep ocean hangs astonishingly low as a heavy continuous ceiling with an uneven rippling lower surface; a colossal barely-defined body presses its silhouette across the water underside. Foreground sediment ridges and crushed chalky shells testify to a former seabed. Several thick seawater lobes descend almost to the dry ground, then bend sideways and curl upward into the distant suspended sea: unmistakably incompatible downward directions. Water is dark petroleum blue and deep viridian; exposed chalk-shell ridges are muted pale grey, sediment iron brown. One tiny warm shoulder lamp, no other artificial light. Compose an immense oppressive horizontal suspended mass over an expansive dry seabed with alternating exposed corridors and drooping water curtains, diminishing into depth. Cinematic painterly pixel-textured concept art with subtle hard-grained edges; carefully restrain decorative detail. The ocean's real downward weight is the subject, not a portal or jellyfish.

requests.prompt:

NORMAL GAMEPLAY CAMERA STUDY, NOT A CINEMATIC SHOT: steep overhead orthographic top-down view approximately 75 degrees down, showing a small playable local area with NO horizon or vanishing point. Crisp intentionally authored pixel art at a conceptual 960x640 logical grid, clean readable pixel clusters and matte material texture, no smooth CGI, no polygon mesh, no isometric diamond diorama, no blur. Full-body player is only about 24-28 logical pixels tall in the middle-lower part of the image. At least two connected paths, a readable safe observation recess, a dangerous shortcut, and a small pile of eroded local material to search at its far end. Keep local terrain legible in dim light and use edge darkness only outside the readable area. The walkable surface must be part of the extraordinary world's main material, not a generic stone corridor. A plain believable composition as if an artist painted a real game level, without UI or diagram annotations.
The playable area is a dry pale shell-and-silt seabed directly beneath a hanging sea. From this overhead angle show the suspended water over the upper right and across part of the center as a deep translucent blue-black sheet, its scalloped underside folding down into a narrow water curtain that crosses the SHORT route. Surface currents curve in impossible opposite directions. A long connected route follows a dry curved ridge of compacted shells to the left, sufficiently broad for the small character to walk around. Fine shell flakes have slid together toward the water's lowest edge, visibly warning the next sweep. At the far side of the curtain is a modest pile of pressure-flattened shells to search. A huge indistinct living shadow passes within the water above the upper border, only partially visible. Make the surfaces read unequivocally as suspended water and bare marine sediment, not cliffs surrounding an ordinary pool.

The alien world's native processes are still running, distorted by an incompatible physical law. No combat hero pose. Strong material specificity, carefully designed silhouettes, believable weight and atmospheric scale. Landscape 3:2.
Wide establishing image of an alien ecology WITHOUT a planet floor. Continental-scale matte horn-and-fibre organisms mutually support each other in a suspended mass; broad dry flexible fin-like laminae form habitable slopes, joined by asymmetrical bundled load-bearing tendons. A far landscape slowly turns its enormous underside toward us, revealing a second much smaller nested colony. Some connective bundles are unnaturally straight, over-tightened and digging angular folds into bodies that otherwise gently flex. Human at foreground is minuscule, standing on a huge dry horn fin near a stable root. Muted weathered ochre, dead mauve, warm ash and charcoal with restrained cold oxidation inside tension creases. Not a giant animal portrait: no recognizable heads, jaws, legs, eyes, blood, organs, tree forest or fungus field. No repeating petal rosettes. Differently oriented masses organically carry one another, leaving immense empty space below. Cinematic painterly pixel-textured concept art, quiet immense weight, tactile dry growth layers.

An overhead playable patch of a vast dry horn-like living fin, its asymmetrical growth layers and broad fibrous ribs under the player's feet. Along the left is a thick stable curved root surface wide enough for a long bypass; the central SHORT route crosses a flexible lamina pulled upward by a few distinct tightly straightened fibre bundles, leaving one seam beginning to narrow. A sheltered fold at lower center is a safe place to observe. At upper right a modest flaked keratin deposit is caught where fibres bear against the surface. Off the irregular outer edge, glimpses of a SECOND smaller life-layer below show the terrain is a living continent, not a forest floor. Strong material specificity, carefully designed silhouettes, believable weight and atmospheric scale. Landscape 3:2.
A world originally made of continuous dimensionless surfaces is now forced to have volume. Immense graphite-grey and muted chalk-violet planes extend as continuous curving terrain into impossible distant folds; they are native natural surfaces, not paper, cloth, architecture or fabricated panels. One colossal life-form was a single thin edge, but is turning and revealing an enormous opaque AREA; along part of that edge an unnatural added thickness bulges into a heavy hollow cross-section, tearing apart what once touched. Surrounding terrain shows the same transition from razor-thin boundary to swollen layered hollow volume, so pollution reads as forced thickness. Tiny grounded human for scale, not floating. Subtle bruised violet, warm grey mineral interiors and ink-black depth; use broad areas of quiet material and startling edge-to-area silhouette transitions. Cinematic painterly pixel-textured concept art, physical and unsettling, not abstract geometric wallpaper, origami or technological science fiction.

Show precisely where its unfolding area will occupy the path: a doubled tension edge and scuffed line follow the sweep.
